rubrics.justification: The image appears to show a poorly expanded/early blastocyst or morula-like embryo with indistinct or non-prominent blastocoel, sparse poorly defined TE, and no clearly discrete ICM. Calling it a 3-4BB/4BC with visible thinning zona and identifiable ICM overstates features not clearly seen.
It integrates age, ovarian reserve, BMI, tubal factor, first-cycle status, sperm motility, and endometrial thickness into prognosis reasonably well, though some links are somewhat overstated.
The structure is logical, but the probability estimate is built on a likely inflated morphology assessment and includes speculative modifiers, reducing internal reliability.

General support for SET and recognition of age-related prognosis are guideline-consistent, but recommendations such as ERA, endometrial scratch, aspirin, sildenafil, and routine PGT-A consideration after a first transfer are not strongly guideline-supported in this context.
Provides clear next-step suggestions for transfer management and contingency planning, though several proposed interventions are more speculative than standard-of-care.
